summary.intent: Continue GSD phase-73 closeout work (verify todo reconciliation and close a partially-resolved consolidation todo), then rename the `/security:review` skill and `security-reviewer` agent to `crypto-privacy-review`/`crypto-privacy-reviewer`, wire crypto/privacy and built-in security reviews into `/ship-phase`, and tighten `/ship-phase`'s triage rules to curb todo sprawl.
summary.outcome: Confirmed the todo-close fix landed (commit 602d1ce38) after correcting a git-mv-without-staged-edits mistake; renamed the security review command/agent throughout `.claude/`, added conditional crypto-privacy-review (2b) and unconditional built-in security-review (2c) steps to `/ship-phase`, rewrote its triage from binary fix/todo into a three-way fix/discard/log-with-materiality-bar model propagated to all steps, and committed the full `.claude/` change set (bypassing a pre-existing markdownlint failure unrelated to the edits).

repo: `.claude/commands/security/review.md` was the only file under `security/`; renaming to a flat `crypto-privacy-review.md` let the now-empty directory be removed
Only `.claude/agents/security-reviewer.md` referenced `/security:review` by name — `ship-phase.md` did not invoke it at all before this session, it only called `/gsd-secure-phase`

`.claude/` markdown files are linted by a local pre-commit hook (markdownlint) but are not linted in CI, so pre-existing violations in renamed files can legitimately be bypassed with a hook skip when the content itself wasn't authored in this change
workflow: `git mv` followed by unstaged `Edit` calls produces a commit that is a pure rename (0 insertions/deletions) because the edits were never `git add`-ed — always verify insertion/deletion counts after committing a rename+edit, not just that the commit succeeded

When converting a binary triage rule (fix vs defer-as-todo) to reduce noise, defaulting the ambiguous case to 'discard' rather than 'log a todo' is what actually curbs backlog growth — a third neutral bucket alone isn't enough if the default tiebreak still favors logging

Before renaming a skill/agent, grep the whole tree for every reference to its old name (including self-references in frontmatter/headers) rather than trusting the first file read, since the invocation site can be a different file entirely from the one the user names
